subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Near-Earth Asteroids
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Near-Earth Asteroids.

hook.text: Over 34,000 asteroids orbit near Earth. Most are harmless, but a few could devastate entire regions.

buildup.text: NASA tracks them constantly. Any asteroid larger than 140 meters could cause catastrophic damage.

discovery.text: In 2022, NASA's DART mission hit asteroid Dimorphos and changed its orbit. Planetary defense works.

twist.text: We've found most large ones. The real danger is the smaller asteroids we haven't detected yet.

climax.text: The Chelyabinsk meteor in 2013 injured 1,500 in Russia. It was just 20 meters wide—with no warning.

punchline.text: We can deflect them now. Finding them first is the hard part.

quiz.question: What did NASA's DART mission prove?
options: That we can change an asteroid's orbit by deliberately crashing into it
That asteroids are made of loose rubble that falls apart easily
That nuclear weapons are the best way to deflect an asteroid

details.summary: Near-Earth asteroids (NEAs) are asteroids whose orbits bring them close to Earth's orbit. Over 32,000 have been discovered, including about 2,300 potentially hazardous asteroids larger than 140 meters.
details.whyItMatters: Unlike most space threats, asteroid impacts are preventable with enough warning. Cataloging NEAs and developing deflection technology is humanity's first effort to protect Earth from a natural catastrophe that has caused mass extinctions before.
takeaways: Over 32,000 near-Earth asteroids have been discovered
About 2,300 are potentially hazardous objects larger than 140 meters
NASA's DART mission proved we can deflect an asteroid

faq.question: How much warning would we have before an impact?
faq.answer: For large asteroids (1 km+), current surveys would likely detect them years to decades in advance. For smaller ones (140 meters), gaps in our catalog mean some could arrive with little warning. Smaller objects (like the 2013 Chelyabinsk meteor at 20 meters) can arrive completely undetected.

faq.question: How did the DART mission work?
faq.answer: On September 26, 2022, NASA deliberately crashed a spacecraft into Dimorphos, a 160-meter moon of asteroid Didymos. The impact shortened Dimorphos's orbit by 33 minutes — far more than the minimum 73-second goal. This proved kinetic impactor deflection works and can be scaled up if needed.
